title: Application of NiP Alloy for the Production of Conductive and Resistive Layers
content: This article presents the use of NiP alloy-based layers for the production of conductive and resistive layers. The authors demonstrate the potential of this technology for the production of electrodes in photovoltaic structures, for example. To facilitate this use of NiP alloy metallization, the authors developed a selective metallization process. Additionally, to simplify the process, process modeling was performed, enabling the rapid selection of chemical metallization process parameters. The use of ultrasound-assisted electroless metallization technology shortens the production time of silicon electrodes for photovoltaic cells. Furthermore, it is possible to produce a metallic layer on flexible substrates. The technology developed by the authors enables the production of electrodes used in flexible photovoltaic cells, for example. The advantage of this type of metallization is its low cost and simplicity. An additional advantage of the presented process is the ability to produce both the top and bottom electrodes in a single process, offering a wide range of industrial applications. Previous work by the authors demonstrated the feasibility of applying the process to typical ceramic and silicon substrates. The work is in line with current research trends aimed at reducing the production costs of photovoltaic cells and, consequently, reducing the carbon footprint associated with production.
